content: tailwind-canonicalize is a production-grade CLI and library that rewrites Tailwind utility classes into their theme-canonical form — only when the result is provably identical . It is not a linter and not a general formatter. It sits beside Biome, ESLint, Oxlint, and Prettier without fighting them. Three transformation categories | Category | What | Safety | |----------|------|--------| | Canonical class | Arbitrary values → theme tokens | Automatic when exact | | Tailwind migration | e.g. bg-gradient-to-br → bg-linear-to-br | Versioned registry | | Semantic tokens | bg-white → bg-background | Analyze + approved manifest only | Goals Zero false positives Unknown values, calc(), var(), and multi-match ambiguity are never rewritten. Coverage is secondary to safety. Theme-driven Loads project @theme (v4) or tailwind.config. (v3). Never hardcodes your design system. Format-preserving Uses MagicString and a real AST (oxc). Comments, multiline class strings, and non-class code stay intact. Ecosystem-friendly First-class integration guides for Biome, ESLint, Oxlint, Prettier, and CI. Next steps - Installation - CLI reference - Interactive examples - Safety contract - Semantic tokens

Core options | Flag | Description | |------|-------------| | --write / -w | Write rewrites to disk | | --check | Exit 1 if changes would be made | | --stdin | Read source from stdin → stdout | | --json | Machine-readable summary | | --verbose | Full −/+ rewrite blocks + every diagnostic line | | --diff | Line diffs | | -o, --report <file | Write human report (plain text, no ANSI) to a file. Requires a path (--report report.txt or --report=report.txt). --report -h is invalid — use -h alone for help. | | --safe | Exact/safe only (default mode) | | --review | Report only; never write | | --aggressive | Review-level migrations / high-confidence inference | Tokens / style report | Command | Description | |---------|-------------| | tokens analyze [paths…] | Propose semantic color mappings (no writes) | | tokens apply <manifest [--write] | Apply approved mappings + optional theme CSS | | tokens report [paths…] | Style usage report v2 — color frequency, byFile/tags, health, CSS theme scan, workflow suggestions (-o styles-report.json, --md styles.md); paths always POSIX | Migrations | Flag | Description | |------|-------------| | --migrate | Apply versioned class renames | | --migrations-only | Skip arbitrary canonicalization | | --from-tailwind <n | Source major (e.g. 3) | | --to-tailwind <n | Target major (e.g. 4) | Performance | Flag | Description | |------|-------------| | --watch | Watch mode (+ incremental) | | --incremental | Hash cache skip | | --workers | Force worker pool | | --concurrency <n | Parallelism (default 8) | Compile verification | Flag | Description | |------|-------------| | --strict-compile | Require Tailwind compile equality | | --compile-css | CSS entry for compiler | Exit codes | Code | Meaning | |------|---------| | 0 | Success | | 1 | Changes required (--check) | | 2 | Error | Conflicts & diagnostics Utilities that share a cascade slot (same property group + variants) but differ in value are reported, never rewritten . - Default report groups identical conflicts by property group (counts + top pairs). - --verbose lists sample diagnostic lines per message. - Conflicts do not block other rewrites in the same file. See Safety for true vs false-positive conflict examples (prose + prose-sm, gradient position vs color, flex + grid). Example output JSON shape

content: Is this a linter? No. It rewrites Tailwind utilities when equivalence is proven. Use Biome/ESLint/Oxlint for lint. Will it break my design? Only rewrites that match your theme (or approved token map) apply. Ambiguous cases are left alone. Does it sort classes? No. Use prettier-plugin-tailwindcss or eslint-plugin-tailwindcss for ordering. Can it invent semantic tokens automatically? Analyze proposes; apply requires an approved manifest. Default mode never auto-applies semantics. v3 and v4? v4 @theme first. v3 tailwind.config. is loaded when no CSS theme is found. Migrations cover common v3→v4 renames. Monorepo? Yes — pass package paths, use --workers, and per-package scripts. Theme discovery uses project CSS/config near cwd.
title: FAQ

content: What rewrites Spacing, sizing, radius, font size, keywords, fractions — with variants and ! preserved. How equivalence works 1. Parse utility structure 2. Resolve active theme (@theme or defaults) 3. Normalize lengths (px ↔ rem at root 16) 4. Match scale keys 5. Require a single safe candidate Optional: --strict-compile uses Tailwind’s compile() API when installed. Conflicts are separate Canonical rewrites never “pick a winner” when two classes set the same cascade slot (max-w-40 + max-w-44, flex + grid). Those are diagnostics only. Unrelated co-occurring classes (prose + prose-sm, from-50% + from-popover) share different property groups and stay quiet — see Safety.

content: Semantic replacements are architectural , not purely canonical. The same bg-amber-200 may mean warning, selection, or decoration — so inference never auto-writes. Phase 1 — Analyze No source edits. Outputs proposals, conflicts, duplicate token reports, cycles. Style usage report (drift) — v2 Inventory all color utilities (not only bg- ) — text-black, bg-slate-200, border- , ring- , fill- , gradients, semantic tokens like text-muted-foreground — with HTML/JSX tag attribution: JSON includes (paths always POSIX: src/components/..., never src\\...): - utilities[] — count, channel, kind (palette | semantic | arbitrary), variants, tags, files, samples - byTag[] / byFile[] / byDirectory[] — reverse indexes and hotspots - summary.health — 0–100 score + semantic/palette ratios - summary.byPalette / byShade / byVariant — rollups - theme — CSS / @theme color tokens, unused vars, missing vars for semantic utilities - suggestions[] — workflow hooks (add-css-color-token, file hotspots, …) for updating globals.css - drift[] — multi-color tags, palette mix, unused/missing theme tokens, file hotspots Never rewrites source. Feed suggestions + theme.missingForSemanticUtilities into token/CSS generators, then re-run the report. Phase 2 — Apply Only explicit mappings, pairs, and recipes in the manifest. Dark pairs when the pair is approved and dual-theme values exist. Theme CSS Generates Tailwind v4 @theme / @theme inline with optional :root + .dark app variables. Prefers aliasing existing --warning-subtle over inventing duplicates.

content: Contract A rewrite is applied only when exactly one theme candidate matches after value normalization (or a registered migration / approved mapping applies). | Situation | Behavior | |-----------|----------| | 0 candidates | Leave untouched | | 1 candidate | Rewrite | | \ 1 candidates | Leave untouched (unless documented preference, e.g. 1/2 over 2/4) | | calc / var / min / max / clamp | Never | | Arbitrary properties [mask-image:…] | Never | | Semantic palette → token | Never without approved manifest | Modes | Mode | Flag | Applies | |------|------|---------| | Safe | --safe (default) | Exact canonical + safe migrations + approved tokens + dups | | Review | --review | Report/diff only | | Aggressive | --aggressive | Explicit; may include review migrations / high-confidence inference | Conflict diagnostics (not rewrites) The engine also detects true cascade conflicts — two utilities that set the same CSS slot with different values. Those are reported only (never auto-resolved). Unrelated utilities that merely share a prefix must not show up as conflicts. Classification uses property-group identity (value-aware where needed): | Classes | Conflict? | Why | |---------|-----------|-----| | prose prose-sm | No | Typography: bare prose enables the plugin; prose-sm is a size modifier (co-occur by design) | | prose-sm prose-lg | Yes | Two prose sizes | | before:from-50% before:from-popover | No | Gradient stop position vs color | | from-red-500 from-blue-500 | Yes | Two gradient-from colors | | font-mono font-medium | No | Font family vs weight | | flex flex-col | No | Display vs direction | | flex grid | Yes | Both set display | | max-w-40 max-w-44 | Yes | Same width slot | If you still see a false conflict, file an issue — property groups are intentionally expanded as real-world class strings surface. Idempotence Unsafe counter CLI always reports unsafe: 0 for rewrites — the engine refuses ambiguous rewrites rather than guessing. Conflict counts are separate (conflicts in the summary) and never rewrite source.
description: Zero false positives — the core product contract.
title: Safety

content: No rewrites happen - Confirm classes are in supported positions (className, clsx, cn, …) - Check theme load (--verbose or JSON themeSource) - Incompatible units like w-[10vh] and calc() / var() — intentional CI fails with exit 1 Why do I see “conflicts detected”? Conflicts mean two utilities compete for the same cascade slot with different values. They are not rewritten — you choose which class to keep in source. Common true conflicts: - flex + grid (both set display) - max-w-40 + max-w-44 - prose-sm + prose-lg Common non-conflicts (should not appear): - prose + prose-sm (enable + size) - from-50% + from-popover (gradient position + color) - font-mono + font-medium (family + weight) Default output groups diagnostics by property group; use --verbose for sample lines. Details: Safety. Cache seems stale Delete .tailwind-canonicalize-cache.json or change options (options hash invalidates). Conflicts with Biome/Prettier Run canonicalize then format. Don’t enable two tools that rewrite the same class strings. Semantic tokens not applied Ensure tokens apply + manifest path, or config tokens.enabled + manifest. Safe mode never invents mappings. --help has no color Color is on only for TTY stdout. NO COLOR=1 always disables; FORCE COLOR=1 forces ANSI even when piped.
